scope: principal two-derivative pure-TT quadratic sector only; algebraic background mass terms, scalar/vector mixing away from pure TT, higher-spatial-derivative UV operators, radiative stability and compact-object sectors are excluded

derivation.polarization_matrix: h_ij=[[hp,hx,0],[hx,-hp,0],[0,0,0]] for a Fourier mode along z
derivation.kinetic: For N=1 and zero shift, K_ij=(eps/2) dot(h_ij). TT tracelessness makes K start at O(eps^2), hence K^2 has no quadratic principal term and (K_ij K^ij-K^2)_(2)=eps^2 Tr(dot h^2)/4.
derivation.gradient: After the standard TT spatial integration by parts, [sqrt(g) R]_(2)=-eps^2 (partial_k h_ij)^2/4. For the z-Fourier mode this is -eps^2 k^2 Tr(h^2)/4.
derivation.scalar_PX: P(X_U) contains no derivatives of the spatial metric, so it cannot alter the principal TT kinetic or gradient coefficients; algebraic background terms are outside this principal-symbol gate.
derivation.mixed_operator: For homogeneous Sigma(t), D_i Sigma=0 and Theta_U=dot(Sigma)/N. In pure TT the lapse and invariant shift are unperturbed at principal quadratic order, so D_i Theta_U=0 and C(X_U) D_i Theta_U D^i Theta_U vanishes identically in this sector.

interpretation: On the fixed IR representative, the explicit rolling-scalar mixed operator does not modify the principal pure-TT kinetic or gradient term. The two-derivative TT cone is the GR cone, c_T^2=1, within the frozen scope.

verification.method: exact symbolic algebra with SymPy using rtk/route_b_u1_fixed_ir_tt_principal_gate.py

non_claims: no compact-object or X_U->0 regularity certification
no statement about algebraic background TT mass terms off shell
